items.abstract: <jats:p>Large multimodal models are now able to operate a computer by perceiving the rendered screen and issuing low-level mouse and keyboard actions, a capability that removes the dependence on a bespoke programming interface for every application. The capability is powerful, yet it carries two structural costs. Every execution re-derives the same visual reasoning, and the resulting action stream is fragile because a pixel coordinate carries no semantic anchor. The presented study introduces WEAVER, a framework that positions an experiential memory layer between a vision-language agent and a live browser so that the agent and the human operator function as resource integrators co-creating a reusable automation asset. WEAVER records each interaction together with a Document Object Model selector inferred from the click coordinate, and it weights that selector by an expected stability score. On replay it applies a tri-modal resolution cascade that attempts the learned selector first, then a visibletext match, and only then the raw coordinate, so that the costly model loop becomes a fallback rather than the default path. A keyword-overlap retrieval step surfaces similar past workflows and supplies them as planning context for new tasks. Conforming to a design-science orientation, the framework was instantiated as a working prototype that drives Chromium through the Claude Computer Use interface, with capability-aware provider routing and a human-in-the-loop control gate for verification challenges. A pilot evaluation over a fixed suite of twenty web tasks recorded a replay success rate of 96.3 percent, with the learned selector alone resolving 71 percent of clicks and the model loop invoked on under one task in ten. The mean step count fell relative to a pixel-only baseline. The study positions the confidenceweighted grounding mechanism, the graded degradation cascade, and the memory-conditioned planner as the principal contributions, and it discusses the scalability, security, and responsible-artificialintelligence implications for enterprise deployment.</jats:p>
title: A Memory-Augmented Browser Automation Framework with Confidence-Weighted Selector Grounding and Tri-Modal Resolution for Resilient Computer-Use Agents
